cards.title: Share what you know — from one room to anywhere!
cards.takeaway: Online teaching lets you teach mathematics, coding, tailoring, languages, or exam prep to learners anywhere using simple free tools.
cards.body: You do **not** need a TV studio to teach online well! Clear explanations, structured short lessons, and choosing the **right teaching mode** matter far more than expensive cameras.

cards.title: The 4 Modes of Online Teaching
cards.takeaway: Match the mode to the learner: Live (real-time), Recorded/Self-paced (watch anytime), Cohort (group starting & finishing together), and One-to-One (personal coaching).
cards.body:
Every online class uses one (or a blend) of **four teaching modes**:
1. **Live (Synchronous):** Teacher and learners meet at the same hour on Zoom / Google Meet. *Advantage:* instant Q&A energy. *Limitation:* network drops or busy work schedules can make learners miss class.
2. **Recorded (Self-paced):** Pre-recorded videos learners watch anytime (even at midnight!), pause, and replay.
3. **Cohort:** A group starts Week 1 together and finishes Week 6 together with shared milestones and accountability (ideal for a 6-week church or bootcamp class!).
4. **One-to-One:** Personal weekly tutoring/mentoring tailored to one student.

check.prompt: Which mode fits a busy nurse who wants to watch lessons at midnight after shift, pause to take notes, and replay tricky parts?

choices.text: Live-only morning class with no replay

check.hint: She needs complete freedom over time, pausing, and rewatching.
check.explanation: Spot on! Recorded self-paced lessons shine whenever learners need flexible hours and replay control.

cards.title: Free tools that cover your entire classroom
cards.takeaway: Zoom / Google Meet hosts live calls, OBS records your screen, Canva designs slides, YouTube (Unlisted) hosts videos free, and Google Forms runs quizzes.
cards.body:
Match each free tool to its exact job:
- **Zoom / Google Meet:** Hosting live video classes or 1-to-1 tutoring calls.
- **OBS Studio (or Loom):** Recording your screen and voice cleanly on your laptop.
- **Canva:** Designing clear visual slides without walls of tiny text.
- **YouTube (Unlisted):** Free, data-friendly video hosting where only students with your link can watch!
- **Google Forms:** Collecting quick quizzes, assignments, and feedback.

check.prompt: A church wants 30 members to start a 6-week study together on Week 1, discuss weekly, and graduate together on Week 6. Which mode fits best?

choices.text: Cohort mode — everyone progresses through the 6 weeks together with shared community accountability
Unscheduled solo reading with zero group contact

check.hint: When a group starts together, moves week-by-week together, and finishes together, what do we call that mode?
check.explanation: Exactly! Cohort courses combine structure, deadlines, and peer encouragement so completion rates soar.

cards.title: Keep lessons short, audio clear, and data bills friendly!
cards.takeaway: Good sound matters more than 4K video — record in a quiet room, keep video chunks 5–12 minutes long, and always check understanding.
cards.body: Learners forgive a modest webcam, yet they close a lesson immediately if audio echoes or hisses! Speak close to your microphone in a quiet room (curtains/clothes absorb echo!) and break 1-hour lectures into crisp 8-minute videos.

check.prompt: Which free tool pair is best for (1) recording your computer screen offline and (2) hosting class videos privately via a shareable link at ₦0?

choices.text: OBS Studio for recording + YouTube (Unlisted) for hosting
Notepad for recording + Calculator for hosting

check.hint: OBS records crisp screen lessons locally, and Unlisted YouTube links stream smoothly on Nigerian mobile networks!
check.explanation: 100% right! OBS + Unlisted YouTube gives any teacher a professional ₦0 video classroom.
